title: Authorization Mapping Shim: Compatibility Layer & Migration Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This document describes a compatibility shim and migration checklist to move from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 without large-scale service disruption. It centralizes the mapping strategy, audit/logging adjustments, evidence automation hooks, and SIEM export considerations so product, SRE, and security teams can run a coordinated rollout.

Scope and goals:
- Support incremental migration of tenants and services from the legacy role model to RBAC v2 permission sets.
- Preserve runtime authorization behavior until new permissions are validated for each route.
- Emit audit events that capture mapping decisions and provide evidence for compliance artifacts.
- Ensure SIEM exports include both pre- and post-migration attributes for correlation.
- Minimize blast radius; enable fast rollback.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full rewrite of service authorization code. The shim is temporary and intended to live in the auth gateway and control plane.
- Not responsible for fine-grained policy language design; it operates on role-to-permission mapping provided by policy owners.

High-level design:
1) Interception layer (compat-shim):
   - Deployed as a sidecar in the auth gateway and as a lightweight library for private deployments.
   - On each authorization request, shim consults: (a) existing v1 role header (if present), (b) a mapping table service (Mapping API), (c) the v2 permission evaluation result when enabled.
   - Decision flow: if tenant flagged as v2-enabled, evaluate v2 permissions. If evaluation fails or mapping absent, fallback to mapped v1->v2 policy produced by the Mapping API.

2) Mapping API (authoritative mapping store):
   - Small internal service owned by security team that hosts canonical mappings, versioned mapping sets, and migration flags per org/service.
   - Exposes endpoints: GET /mapping?role=..., POST /mapping-set (for staged mappings), GET /mapping-sets (versions).
   - Mappings are immutable once activated; new mapping-sets are created for iterative corrections.

3) Audit & evidence emission:
   - Audit events must include the following common fields: timestamp, request_id, principal_id, tenant_id, route, resource, decision (allow/deny), source_model (v1|v2|mapping_shim), mapping_set_id (if used), mapping_rule_id (if applicable), evaluation_latency_ms, fallback_reason (if any).
   - Example event (log line):
     { ts: "2025-02-13T14:22:31Z", rid: "req_abc", principal: "svc-data-processor", tenant: "acme", route: "/models/generate", resource: "model:open-13b", decision: "allow", source_model: "mapping_shim", mapping_set_id: "mapset-20250210-01", mapping_rule_id: "map-roles-12", eval_ms: 4 }
   - The shim must write both structured JSON audit events to the platform audit stream and an evidence blob to the evidence-s3 bucket containing: request headers, mapped role list, raw v2 policy evaluation output (if available), and a short human-readable rationale. Blob path convention: evidence/tenant_id/YYYY/MM/DD/req_id.json

Mapping model and examples:
- Mapping primitives: role -> [permission_ids], permission_id is the canonical unit consumed by RBAC v2.
- Support role aliases and hierarchical role expansion (legacy roles often implied other roles).
- Example mapping table snippet (conceptual):
   legacy:admin -> [perm:org:read, perm:org:write, perm:secrets:read]
   legacy:read-only -> [perm:org:read]
   analytics:etl -> [perm:data:read, perm:compute:job:run]

- Conflict resolution rules:
  * Explicit mappings win over heuristic inference.
  * If a legacy role maps to an empty permission set, reject activation for that mapping_set until resolved.
  * Mapping API will mark ambiguous mappings with a review_required flag.

Evidence automation and linkage to audits:
- Evidence artifacts are created per-request for a configurable sampling rate during early phases (default 100% for canaries, 5% for staged tenants, 0.1% platform-wide).
- Evidence includes provenance metadata: mapping_set_id, mapping_version, who last edited mapping_set (user/email), Jira ticket reference for mapping changes.
- Evidence automation tasks:
  1) On evidence creation, send message to kafka topic evidence-created.v1 with attributes: tenant_id, req_id, evidence_path, mapping_set_id.
  2) Evidence ingestion pipeline (Airflow job) enriches blob with additional context (org tier, SLA, recent incidents) and copies to evidence-store for retention and compliance export.
  3) Retention policy: default 180 days; extended retention for flagged tenants per compliance agreements.

SIEM export and schema compatibility:
- SIEM export must preserve both v1 and v2 context fields during transition. Recommended flattened event fields for SIEM consumers:
  * event_time, event_id, tenant_id, principal, route, resource, decision, source_model, mapping_set_id, v1_role (optional), v2_permission_list (optional), evidence_ref, org_tier, eval_latency_ms
- A stable event id (request_id) ensures SIEM correlation when events are split across streams (gateway vs mapping service).
- For backward compatibility, a compatibility adapter will produce legacy-style fields for existing SIEM dashboards: legacy_role= v1_role (when available), legacy_decision=decision. This adapter is configured per-SIEM-connector and will be toggled via feature flag.

Deployment and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0: Preparation (2–3 weeks)
  - Inventory of services that use v1 roles (automated scan + manual validation). (JIRA-AUTH-210)
  - Publish canonical permission catalog and initial mapping draft for top 15 roles.
  - Build Mapping API minimal endpoints and shim sidecar prototype.
  - Add audit fields to audit schema and notify SIEM team of new fields.
  - Create smoke test suite (see Smoke tests section).

Phase 1: Internal dogfood canary (1 week)
  - Enable shim for internal platform services only; mapping_set = mapset-internal-01.
  - Evidence sampling = 100%.
  - Run smoke tests + production load tests. Monitor: authorization error rate, median eval latency, SIEM event completeness.

Phase 2: Customer canaries (2–4 weeks)
  - Work with 3–5 friendly customers (low-risk) to enable v2 evaluation in parallel with v1.
  - Mapping owners create tenant-specific mapping_set; mapping edits gated by PRs and JIRA references.
  - Evidence sampling = 100% for these tenants.
  - Observe mismatch rate between v1 and v2 decisions. For any mismatch >1% on critical routes, pause and investigate.

Phase 3: Progressive rollout (rolling, weeks–months)
  - Gradually enable mapping_shim fallback for broader tenants in cohorts (by traffic and complexity).
  - Reduce evidence sampling for cohorts after 2 weeks of stability.
  - Add automation to create mapping tickets when ambiguous mappings observed.

Phase 4: Cutover and cleanup
  - For tenants with low mismatch rates and validated mappings, flip tenant flag to v2-first mode (v2 evaluated first, fallback to mapping only on error).
  - After 90 days of stability, deprecated v1 headers and legacy adapter paths will be scheduled for removal.

Rollback strategy:
- Each deployment carries a kill-switch feature flag at the gateway and Mapping API level. Immediate rollback steps:
  1) Flip global feature flag to enable v1-only path.
  2) Revoke newly created mapping_set activations performed in the last 24h.
  3) Notify on-call SRE and security lead.
  4) Re-run smoke tests to confirm baseline.

Smoke tests and success metrics:
- Authorization success rate (should not drop more than 0.1% during rollout).
- Mapping mismatch rate: percent of requests where v1 and v2 disagree (target <0.5% before cutover).
- Audit completeness: percent of requests with evidence_ref present in audit events (target 99%).
- Eval latency 95p must not increase by >20ms for gateway-critical routes.
- SIEM ingestion completeness: percentage of events with event_id and evidence_ref (target >99%).

Checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] Mapping API deployed to staging and prod with versioned mapping_sets.
- [ ] Shim sidecar integrated into gateway and packaged for private deployments.
- [ ] Audit schema updates deployed and SIEM team notified.
- [ ] Evidence S3 bucket and kafka topic provisioned and access controlled.
- [ ] Smoke tests and dashboards created: auth-success-rate, mapping-mismatch-rate, evidence-coverage.
- [ ] Runbook for rollback and incident triage created and shared.

Operational runbook (quick commands / checks):
- Disable shim globally: curl -X POST https://ctl.redwood/feature-flags/shim_disable -d '{"env":"prod"}'
- Query mapping for role: curl https://mapping-api.internal/mapping?role=legacy:admin
- Fetch evidence for request: aws s3 cp s3://evidence-bucket/evidence/tenant/2025/02/req_id.json -
- Re-create mapping_set from previous version: POST /mapping-set with body {source: "clone:mapset-20250210-01"} (ops only)

Open questions and risks:
- Long-tail roles: hundreds of rarely-used legacy roles may require heuristics or manual review. Risk: missed permissions during cutover. Mitigation: prioritize high-traffic roles and implement auto-ticketing for low-confidence mappings.
- Data residency concerns for evidence blobs in private deployments. Mitigation: for private deployments route evidence to customer-managed storage and provide a no-exfiltration mode.
- SIEM schema churn: dashboards and detection rules will need updates. Mitigation: provide compatibility adapter and a migration timeline for SOC teams.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Mapping API contract and minimal implementation: Tomás Ortega (due 2025-02-18)
- Shim sidecar POC and integration tests: Priya Kapoor (due 2025-02-20)
- Audit schema change PR and SIEM update: Aisha Mendes (due 2025-02-25)
- Customer canary coordinators + runbook: Jordan Lee (due 2025-03-05)

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- List mapping_sets: curl https://mapping-api.internal/mapping-sets | jq .
- Check active tenants flagged for v2: psql -h auth-db -c "select tenant_id, v2_flag, mapping_set from tenant_migration where v2_flag = true;"
- Sample log query (ELK): index=audit event.source_model:(mapping_shim OR v2) | stats count() by tenant_id, mapping_set_id

Document history:
- 2025-02-12: Draft created (Priya Kapoor)
- 2025-02-18: Added mapping API contract and example events (Tomás Ortega)
- 2025-03-01: Incorporated SIEM export adapter notes and rollout timeline (Aisha Mendes)

End of document.
